A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-index-model study and provide readable main text, equations, figures and appendices. The existing material can be matched reliably, including relocated Figure 1; v2 adds Appendix D and Figure 4.

before.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 1 report original simulations comparing SGD trajectories under PCA, random and fixed initializations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulations and adds an alignment-sensitivity experiment in Appendix D and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The single-layer model, known activation, squared loss, spherical SGD updates, PCA initialization and transfer-learning procedure are retained. Appendix D tests the existing method without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Appendix D extends the synthetic evaluation to weaker spike–target alignment conditions, beyond the original examples with η1 = 0.45 and 1. The Gaussian single-index recovery task and third-Hermite activation remain the same.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains random initialization, PCA initialization and two fixed-initialization configurations in each setting. The new PCA sensitivity analysis introduces no additional comparison method; added related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a controlled alignment sweep with PCA initialization and nominally inherits Section 5.2's settings. Existing experiments retain d = 1000, 1.5 million steps and step size 10^-7. Figure 4 nevertheless extends to 2 million steps, leaving the new experiment's precise budget inconsistent.

E4.justification: The new Appendix D experiment varies spike–target alignment to test when PCA initialization enables recovery and when it fails. This adds a focused sensitivity analysis; the original initialization comparisons and population-flow analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, replicated-run aggregates, confidence intervals or significance tests for the simulations. Figure 1's four trajectories represent different initialization configurations, and Figure 4 adds configurations without changing uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds trajectories where η1 = 0.3–0.5 approaches correlation 1, η1 = 0.2 improves more slowly, and η1 = 0.1 or 0.01 approaches zero. These are new results under varied alignment conditions; the existing Figure 1 trajectories and findings are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly specifies λ > 0 and dimension-independent λ and η1, tightening the stated asymptotic assumptions. The theorem bounds and proofs in Appendices A–C remain unchanged. The added dimension-independence wording for r restates a property already given in v1's Appendix A.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about polynomial sample-complexity benefits and regimes where pre-training overcomes failure from random initialization. The additional experiment supports these claims without expanding their stated scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D interprets weak-alignment failures as insufficient task-relevant information from PCA initialization for recovery on a reasonable timescale. This adds a concrete applicability boundary to v1's discussion of sufficient alignment, without changing the existing explanations of SGD trapping.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Figure 4 document the new sweep's PCA initialization, third-Hermite activation and η1 values of 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 and 0.01, referring to Section 5.2 for other settings. Existing implementation and resource-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Arnaboldi et al., Gerace et al. and Pesce et al., removes Hagos and Kant, and explicitly relates the transfer-learning reduction to Theorem 7 of Mousavi-Hosseini et al. Other apparent reference changes largely update publication metadata. The new single-gradient-step discussion contains unresolved citation keys.

P1.justification: V2 adds short explanations of assumptions and information exponents, Appendix D, an impact statement and an acknowledgment. Citation formatting changes throughout, but the main section sequence and most prose remain intact. Unresolved citation text appears in Section 2.2.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 4 and moves Figure 1 from page 9 to page 14 after the references. Figure 1's upper panels are enlarged and stacked vertically, while its retained caption still describes left/right groupings. Figures 2 and 3 retain their content and arrangement.

improvement.justification: Appendix D provides useful empirical evidence about a limitation of PCA initialization that v1 primarily addressed through sufficient conditions. Clearer assumptions and acknowledgment of closely related transfer-learning results also help. These yield a limited net improvement, tempered by the new experiment's inconsistent time horizon, unresolved citations and Figure 1's mismatched layout and caption; the central theoretical contribution is unchanged.
